reason: This text does not support the statement that priest leaders are superior to non-priest leaders. Rather, Moses—who is not yet formally designated as a priest—is established as the supreme leader and primary mediator between God and the people. Moses receives direct communication from God, mediates the covenant, and issues commands that Aaron (who becomes the high priest) must follow and defer to. Notably, the text explicitly states that the entire people of Israel are to be 'a kingdom of priests and a holy nation' (מַמְלֶכֶת כֹּהֲנִים וְגוֹי קָדוֹשׁ), suggesting a universal priestly calling rather than a hierarchical superiority of priests over other leaders. Aaron's failure in leadership when left temporarily in charge (the golden calf incident) further undermines any notion of inherent priestly superiority in this passage.
